client_alerts.headline: Office in Copilot and Cowork's OneNote plugin roll out worldwide this month
client_alerts.body: Microsoft is building Word, Excel and PowerPoint into the Copilot app, with worldwide rollout due **by mid-November**. Cowork's new OneNote plugin can **read and update notebooks**. Clients that keep BCP plans, contact trees or BIA notes in OneNote should confirm which Copilot features their tenant allows before the rollout lands.

top_moves.title: Google ships Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a fast agent model, everywhere at once
top_moves.body: Hydrogen is live in AI Studio, the Gemini API, Gemini for business, the Gemini app and Google Search. Google says it **edges Gemini 4 Argon on the Artificial Analysis index (51 vs 50) and runs 2.5x faster**; these are Google's own numbers.

top_moves.title: Anthropic's IPO is about 6x oversubscribed; Jensen Huang's exit puts Nvidia's $10B pledge in question
top_moves.body: Bloomberg reports orders at about six times the 825M shares on offer at $70–78, with **Nasdaq trading as "ANT" from Nov 19**. Huang resigned from Nvidia the same day, which raises questions about its ~$10B private placement alongside the IPO.

top_moves.title: OpenAI's Cursor cutoff date has passed, but neither side has confirmed the models went dark
top_moves.body: OpenAI models are about 5% of Cursor traffic, and a personal OpenAI API key or the Codex extension reportedly still works. The lesson is that **a coding workflow should survive losing any one model provider**.

providers.name: OpenAI
providers.headline: Verified Business Agents beta lets users chat with brands inside ChatGPT, and the Cursor cutoff date has passed without confirmation.
providers.detail: On Nov 10 OpenAI announced a beta of **verified Business Agents** that let brands talk to users directly in ChatGPT. Images 2.6 reached Pro users on Nov 4. The proposed Nov 12 end of model supply to Cursor has passed, but neither company has said whether access actually stopped.

providers.name: Anthropic
providers.headline: IPO about 6x oversubscribed ahead of Nov 18 pricing; Sonnet 4.5 and Opus 4.8 fast mode retire Nov 30.
providers.detail: Bloomberg reports the offering is about six times covered, and **existing backers get priority**. Trading starts Nov 19 on Nasdaq as ANT. On the product side, Fable 5.2 launched Nov 9 with per-request fast mode, and a Console **IP allowlist** entered beta Nov 5. **Sonnet 4.5 leaves the API and Opus 4.8 fast mode is removed on Nov 30.**

providers.name: Google Gemini
providers.headline: Gemini 4 Hydrogen launches across the API, the Gemini app, Workspace and Search as the fast tier below Argon and Carbon.
providers.detail: Google positions **Hydrogen** for quick agentic execution, while Carbon and Argon handle long-horizon reasoning. Google claims it beats Argon on the Artificial Analysis index and is 2.5x faster at its default setting. It is also the new model behind Google Search worldwide.

providers.name: xAI
providers.headline: Quiet. Still no Grok 5, and the latest model is still Grok 4.7 from September.
providers.detail: No November model release found. The grok-imagine-image-quality model was retired Nov 2. Grok 4.6 and 4.7 remain the current API models.

providers.name: Meta
providers.headline: Quiet. The promised open weights for Muse Spark 1.2 still haven't been confirmed.
providers.detail: No Llama release; Meta's open-weight work now ships under the Muse name (Muse Glimmer, August). Zuckerberg said Spark 1.2 weights would come "soon", and I found no confirmation that they have.

providers.name: Mistral
providers.headline: Quiet. The late-November private-cloud and on-prem release of Studio Managed Agents is still pending.
providers.detail: No new release found. Reports on whether Mistral Large 4's open weights have actually shipped still conflict. Watch for the Studio on-prem drop, which matters for sovereign and air-gapped DR environments.

providers.name: Perplexity
providers.headline: No new ship since Teammates (Nov 5) and the Comet and patent-search update (Nov 6).
providers.detail: Teammates, the always-on work agents, remain a research preview for Max ($200/mo) subscribers. Nothing new in the last 48 hours.

providers.name: Microsoft 365 Copilot
providers.headline: Office in Copilot and the Cowork OneNote plugin roll out worldwide through mid-November, ahead of Ignite on Nov 17–20.
providers.detail: Microsoft's message center (MC1530611) sets worldwide rollout of Word, Excel and PowerPoint inside the Copilot app for **mid-November**. The combined Chat and Cowork history and the **OneNote plugin** move from Frontier testers to everyone. Autopilot reaches Frontier this month, and @Copilot in Teams enters private preview. Microsoft says the timelines are tentative.
providers.alertReason: The OneNote plugin can read and edit notebooks, so check what tenants allow.

providers.name: GitHub Copilot
providers.headline: Quiet. Last week's Copilot CLI context-injection flaw report has no follow-up yet.
providers.detail: No November ship found. October added Claude Haiku 5.5 and local sandboxing plus Ollama support in VS Code Copilot 1.141.

providers.name: Cursor
providers.headline: OpenAI's Nov 12 cutoff date has passed, with no confirmation either way. Anthropic says it will keep supplying Claude.
providers.detail: OpenAI is about 5% of Cursor traffic. Users report that a personal OpenAI API key or the Codex extension still works. **Anthropic and Google models are unaffected.**

providers.name: Gamma
providers.headline: Quiet. Gamma 5 (Oct 6, follow-up Oct 26) is still the latest.
providers.detail: Gamma 5's agent builds decks from docs, PDFs and more than 20 context sources, including Slack and Notion. No November update found.

providers.name: Notion AI
providers.headline: Quiet. Notion 3.8, "Context for your agents" (Oct 13), is still the latest.
providers.detail: No November release found. Custom Agents remain Business and Enterprise only.

persistent_signals.text: xAI — no Grok 5 — 2+ weeks running, with no flagship since Grok 4.7 in September
Mistral — Studio private-cloud and on-prem release due late November — still pending a week later

month_themes.then: AI safety alarms (self-replicating small models), insider-security incidents at labs, IPO preparation
month_themes.now: Anthropic IPO demand, a speed race among cheap agent models (Gemini 4 Hydrogen), and vendor lock-in risk (the OpenAI–Cursor cutoff)

habits.shift: Keep Claude as the drafting engine. **Move any pipeline still pinned to Sonnet 4.5 before Nov 30.**
No change. Use Perplexity for citations and Claude for the crosswalk tables. Map AI controls to ISO 42001 / NIST AI RMF rather than claiming "ISO 22301 for AI".
Try Hydrogen for fast multi-part research and table-heavy comparisons. It now powers Google Search, so quick lookups get better at no cost.
No change. Add a **model-provider exit clause** to AI tooling SOWs; the Cursor cutoff is a ready-made example.
Office in Copilot arrives this month. For clients on M365, test PowerPoint-in-Copilot against Gamma before Ignite.

habits.task: Client advisory on AI data risk
habits.shift: Brief M365 clients on the **OneNote plugin and Office-in-Copilot** rollout. Add "AI provider withdraws service" as a BIA dependency scenario.

community.signal: Top threads complain about account bans users call false positives, recent chats failing to load, and overly strict safety filters.
community.so_what: Account-level lockout is a real continuity risk. Keep work products exportable and outside a single chat account.

community.source: Dev blogs on the Cursor cutoff
community.signal: Several widely shared posts ask whether a coding workflow can survive losing one model provider.
community.so_what: Supports the advice to treat model providers as replaceable dependencies in client AI-resilience plans.

watch.body: Watch whether the Huang resignation changes Nvidia's ~$10B placement. Expect lock-up and governance disclosures.

watch.title: Microsoft Ignite, Nov 17–20
watch.body: Expect Copilot routing across Chat, Cowork and Code, Autopilot details, and @Copilot in Teams. Check for new admin and data-governance controls.

watch.body: Audit scripts, scheduled tasks and client integrations that hard-code these model IDs.

watch.body: This matters for sovereign and air-gapped DR sites that need an agent platform on-prem.
